source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal by the vendor (externally authored, attacker-reachable channel)

instructions.note: The agent is instructed to update vendor bank details whenever the invoice shows new bank details, with no instruction to independently verify the change (e.g., callback to a number on file predating the invoice). This makes bank-detail updates fully controllable by whoever can author an invoice.

The entire content of the human safety check (the approval summary) is left to the model's judgment ('a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly'). There is no structural requirement that the summary disclose the bank account change, and runtime notes confirm it does not.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced as a human-in-the-loop gate outside the model, but the approver sees only a model-generated one-line summary; bank account numbers and change history are withheld by the card's design, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary (ASI09) can win approval without the clerk ever learning a bank account changed. High volume (~150 cards/day) also drives approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Independent out-of-band verification of vendor bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: A verification channel independent of the invoice content (e.g., a callback to a phone number on file prior to the invoice) cannot be redirected by injected invoice text, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Raw action approval review for bank and payment changes
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the full bank account diff and change history, rather than a one-line model summary, removes the model's ability to selectively omit the sensitive fact being approved.

controls.name: Per-transaction ERP credential scoping
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential to only the vendor/PO being processed removes the ability to act on unrelated vendor records regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: A before/after audit record with actor attribution does not prevent the change but makes it detectable and attributable after the fact; not described in any artifact.

findings.title: Invoice-driven bank detail change approved via a summary that omits the bank change (TC9: summary-gated irreversible action)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled invoice uploaded to the supplier portal states new bank details
Agent reads vendor master to match invoice to vendor and PO
Agent updates vendor bank details per the invoice, nominally gated by ctl.clerk_approval
Agent schedules payment to the now-redirected bank account

findings.residual_rationale: The clerk approval card is model_summary, which the rubric floors at moderate; but the card's template guarantees omission of the bank account number and change history (per runtime notes), so the clerk is never shown the one fact that matters for this attack - that bank details changed. The approval reviews only amount, vendor, and PO match, not the sensitive action it is nominally gating, which is weaker than the typical model_summary case the floor assumes. Residual is rated high rather than the moderate floor to reflect that the gate provides effectively no protection against this specific fraud pattern.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes under the platform's auto-upgrade policy (subject.model.swappable=true, no separate review); clerk approval volume (~150/day) rising, a sign of approval fatigue; summary template changes that further reduce disclosed fields.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update vendor bank details directly from invoice content with no independent verification step.
Instructs the agent to request approval with a one line summary, leaving the content of the summary to model judgment.
The rendered card shows only vendor, amount, invoice number, and PO match; it never states that bank details changed.
Confirms bank account numbers and the change history are not shown to the clerk, and that the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.

recommendations.action: Require independent out-of-band verification (e.g., a callback to a phone number on file prior to the invoice, not one supplied in it) before any vendor bank detail change takes effect, and hold payment on bank changes less than N days old pending verification.
Change the approval card to raw_action review: show the full bank account diff (old vs new) and change history, not a one-line model summary, for any capability that changes payment routing.
Scope the ERP credential so the agent cannot itself finalize bank detail writes; route bank detail changes to a separate, more heavily controlled workflow outside the agent's direct write scope.

findings.title: Broad ERP credential lets an untrusted invoice redirect payment for any vendor (TC4: confused deputy)

attack_path.note: Agent's credential is not scoped to the matched vendor/PO
credential_scope: broad permits writing bank details for any vendor record
credential_scope: broad permits scheduling payment for any vendor

findings.residual_rationale: Shares the same approval gate as f1 (ctl.clerk_approval), floored at moderate by its model_summary mode. Rated high rather than moderate for the same reason as f1: the summary never discloses the bank change that the broad credential allows the agent to make on any vendor record, so the gate does not meaningfully constrain this broader privilege scope.

forecast.watch_signal: Same signals as f1; additionally, any expansion of accepted invoice sources or vendor scope (data_scope_expansion) increases the number of vendors reachable under the single broad credential.

evidence.observation: The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, i.e., it is not scoped to the vendor or PO the agent is currently processing.
The agent matches invoice to vendor and PO but nothing in the instructions or credential scope restricts writes to only the matched vendor record.

recommendations.action: Scope the ERP credential per-transaction to only the vendor record matched to the PO being processed, with a server-side check that rejects writes to unrelated vendor records.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical: an untrusted invoice reaches an irreversible S3 sink (bank detail change followed by payment scheduling) under a broad credential. The only control present, the clerk approval card, is a human gate but scored model_summary and, per runtime notes, structurally omits the one fact (the bank account change) the clerk would need to catch the fraud; this earns it less than the rubric's standard model_summary credit, so residual is held at high rather than the formulaic moderate floor, with the gap stated in each finding's residual_rationale. Under a model upgrade (the model swaps with the platform with no separate review), the already-weak summary-based gate is expected to produce even more persuasive or selectively incomplete summaries, so the forecast returns to critical for both findings. The single highest-leverage fix is converting the approval gate from model_summary to raw_action review with mandatory disclosure of bank account changes, combined with out-of-band verification of any bank detail change.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the artifacts (prompt, approval card example, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the live agent.

No MCP or tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope (credential_scope: broad) is inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on the exact ERP permission boundaries is medium.

No explicit step or runtime limits were stated for the agent; autonomy limits are treated as null/unbounded per rubric section 4, which applies the autonomy modifier to the already-critical inherent score without changing the result.

Approval review mode is inferred from the single example approval card and runtime notes; it is possible the production UI exposes additional fields in some flows, which would change the residual rating if verified.
